column8: Protocols: We retrospectively obtained de-identified FFPE tissue from patients who underwent ileo-colic resection surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis between 2005 and 2010. CD patient surgical resections were due to complications associated with the disease, whereas control resections were due to adenoma, carcinoma or abdominal trauma. The set of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue sections from each resection were obtained and examined by two pathologists (T.C.L. and T.S.S.) to identify the uninvolved proximal margin (terminal ileum) of each resection. These tissue sections were then further evaluated to identify those that met the histological inclusion criteria for this study. The criteria were that the sample had at least 100 well-oriented intestinal crypts (contained crypt lumens that extended from the apex to the base of the crypt) and absent/minimal active or chronic inflammatory disease (e.g., cryptitis, crypt abscess, architectural distortion, pyloric gland metaplasia, etc.).The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Washington University. Patients were recruited by the Washington University Digestive Diseases Research Core Center (DDRCC). Written informed consent was obtained from all study participants prior to inclusion in the study. For samples that met the histological inclusion criteria, two fresh, unstained 5-µm FFPE tissue sections on glass microscope slides were obtained. Slides were not baked after cutting. For each sample, the two tissue sections were scraped off of the slides using a clean razor and placed in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. The tubes were briefly centrifuged to place the sample towards the bottoms or sides of the tube. RNA extraction and DNase treatment was performed using the RNeasy FFPE kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the Xylene protocol for the paraffin removal step and 30 µL RNase-free H2O for the elution step. RNA was initially quantified by NanoDrop. Subsequent total RNA quantification and quality assessment was performed by Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). Samples were excluded from the study if >20% of the RNA fragments were >200 base pairs in length, as determined with the Bioanalyzer software. Library preparation was performed by the Genome Technology Access Center (GTAC) at Washington University. Library preparation used 150 ng of total RNA. ds-cDNA was generated using the Ovation RNA-seq FFPE system (Nugen, per manufacturer’s instructions). cDNA was blunt ended, had an A base added to the 3’ ends, and then had Illumina sequencing adapters ligated to the ends. Ligated fragments were then amplified for 12 cycles using primers incorporating unique index tags.

column13: Retrieved endometrial samples were immediately placed in RNAlater solution (Thermo Fisher Scientific Baltics UAB, Vilnius, Lithuania), stored overnight at +4 °C and then transferred to –80 °C. column13: Total RNA were extracted from tissues using the RNeasy mini Kit (Qiagen), quantified using a NanoDrop™ 8000 spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific) and quality controlled using a 2100 Electrophoresis Bioanalyzer (Agilent). Libraries of template molecules suitable for strand specific high throughput DNA sequencing were created using “TruSeq Stranded Total RNA with Ribo-Zero Gold Prep Kit” (catalog # RS-122-2301, Illumina Inc.). Briefly, the removal of cytoplasmic and mitochondrial ribosomal RNA (rRNA) was performed from 500 ng of total RNA using biotinylated, target-specific oligos combined with Ribo-Zero rRNA removal beads. Following purification, the RNA was fragmented using divalent cations under elevated temperature. The cleaved RNA fragments were copied into first strand cDNA using reverse transcriptase and random primers, followed by second strand cDNA synthesis using DNA Polymerase I and RNase H. The double stranded cDNA fragments were blunted using T4 DNA polymerase, Klenow DNA polymerase and T4 PNK. A single 'A' nucleotide was added to the 3' ends of the blunt DNA fragments using a Klenow fragment (3' to 5'exo minus) enzyme. The cDNA fragments were ligated to double stranded adapters using T4 DNA Ligase. The ligated products were enriched by PCR amplification (30 sec at 98°C [10 sec at 98°C, 30 sec at 60°C, 30 sec at 72°C] x 12 cycles 5 min at 72°C). Excess of PCR primers was removed by purification using AMPure XP beads (Agencourt Biosciences Corporation). Final cDNA libraries were quality-checked and quantified using a 2100 Electrophoresis Bioanalyzer (Agilent). The libraries were loaded in the flow cell at 7pM concentration and clusters were generated in the Cbot and sequenced in the Illumina Hiseq 2500 as paired-end 2x50 base reads following Illumina's instructions. Image analysis and base calling were performed using RTA 1.17.20 and CASAVA 1.8.2.

column13: During cardiac surgery, a biopsy sample of the RAA was collected from each patient. Tissue samples were collected at the cannulation site, the insertion site of the venous line for the heart–lung machine. Dissected biopsies were briefly washed in ice-cold sterile saline, cut into 0.5 cm thick tissue pieces, and immersed into 3 ml of RNAlater (Sigma Aldrich, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany) to inactivate RNAses and stabilize RNA. Samples were let to stabilize at +4°C for one day and stored at under -70°C until processing. Total RNA was isolated from RAA biopsies via initial ice-cold tissue homogenization using a Precellys 24 tissue homogenizer equipped with the Cryolys cooling option (Bertin Technologies SAS, Montigny-le-Bretonneux, France) followed by RNA isolation using combined QIAzol / chloroform extraction and Qiagen RNeasy mini spin column purification according to the manufacturer's instructions (Qiagen, Venlo, Netherlands). The sample RNA integrity number (RIN mean 7.95 ± 0.55 range 7.1–9.0) and total quantity (mean 3069.55 ± 1141.08 ng range 867.8–6855.0 ng) was evaluated in the Functional Genomics Unit (FuGU, University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland). Briefly, blood was diluted with phosphate buffered saline (PBS Gibco) after plasma collection. The diluted blood was then layered on top of Ficoll-Paque PLUS (Merck). After centrifugation (1200 g, 10 min, brake on), the supernatant was poured into a 50 mL polypropylene tube. Collected PBMCs were washed twice in PBS. PBMCs were counted using a hemacytometer with trypan blue (Lonza) to determine cell viability. Ribonucleic acid (RNA) was prepared using the PureLink RNA Mini kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The total RNA was quantified using Qubit Fluorometer (ThermoFisher Scientific). The purity was checked using NanoPhotometer spectrophotometer (Implen). The integrity and quality of the RNA was assessed using Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100 system (Agilent Technologies) and agarose gel electrophoresis (1% agarose gel, 180 V, 16 min). A total of 2 µg RNA from each sample was subjected to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) removal using Epicentre RiboZeroTM rRNA Removal Kit (Epicentre). The rRNA was cleaned up using ethanol precipitation method. The Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) library was prepared using NEBNext UltraTM Directional RNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina (NEB). In brief, the RNA were fragmented using divalent cations at 94°C in the presence of NEBNext First Strand Synthesis Reaction Buffer and Random Primers. Subsequently, the first strand complementary deoxyribonucleic acid (cDNA) was synthesized using random hexamer and M-MulV reverse transcriptase and the second strand cDNA was synthesized using DNA Polymerase and RNAse H. The dTTP was replaced by dUTP during the second strand cDNA synthesis. The double stranded cDNA fragment was converted to blunt end via end repair reaction and the NEBNext adapter (hairpin loop structure adapter) was ligated to the adenylated cDNA fragment using ligase. Next, the second-strand cDNA was degraded with the aids of USER enzyme. Size selection and sample purification was performed using AMPure XP Beads (Beckman Coulter). Subsequently, Illumina sequencing adapter and indexes were added onto the cDNA fragment via PCR amplification (hereafter known as sequencing library). The sequencing library was purified using Ampure XP Beads (Beckman Coulter). The size distribution of the sequencing library was assessed using Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100 system (Agilent Technologies). The qualified sequencing library was loaded onto NovaSeq 6000 (Illumina) for sequencing using paired-end 150 sequencing strategy. Raw data generated from the sequencer were demultiplexed and converted to FASTQ file using Illumina bcl2fastq.

column8: Protocols: We retrospectively obtained de-identified FFPE tissue from patients who underwent ileo-colic resection surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis between 2005 and 2010. CD patient surgical resections were due to complications associated with the disease, whereas control resections were due to adenoma, carcinoma or abdominal trauma. The set of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue sections from each resection were obtained and examined by two pathologists (T.C.L. and T.S.S.) to identify the uninvolved proximal margin (terminal ileum) of each resection. These tissue sections were then further evaluated to identify those that met the histological inclusion criteria for this study. The criteria were that the sample had at least 100 well-oriented intestinal crypts (contained crypt lumens that extended from the apex to the base of the crypt) and absent/minimal active or chronic inflammatory disease (e.g., cryptitis, crypt abscess, architectural distortion, pyloric gland metaplasia, etc.).The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Washington University. Patients were recruited by the Washington University Digestive Diseases Research Core Center (DDRCC). Written informed consent was obtained from all study participants prior to inclusion in the study. For samples that met the histological inclusion criteria, two fresh, unstained 5-µm FFPE tissue sections on glass microscope slides were obtained. Slides were not baked after cutting. For each sample, the two tissue sections were scraped off of the slides using a clean razor and placed in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. The tubes were briefly centrifuged to place the sample towards the bottoms or sides of the tube. RNA extraction and DNase treatment was performed using the RNeasy FFPE kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the Xylene protocol for the paraffin removal step and 30 µL RNase-free H2O for the elution step. RNA was initially quantified by NanoDrop. Subsequent total RNA quantification and quality assessment was performed by Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). Samples were excluded from the study if >20% of the RNA fragments were >200 base pairs in length, as determined with the Bioanalyzer software. Library preparation was performed by the Genome Technology Access Center (GTAC) at Washington University. Library preparation used 150 ng of total RNA. ds-cDNA was generated using the Ovation RNA-seq FFPE system (Nugen, per manufacturer’s instructions). cDNA was blunt ended, had an A base added to the 3’ ends, and then had Illumina sequencing adapters ligated to the ends. Ligated fragments were then amplified for 12 cycles using primers incorporating unique index tags.

Libraries of template molecules suitable for strand specific high throughput DNA sequencing were created using “TruSeq Stranded Total RNA with Ribo-Zero Gold Prep Kit” (catalog # RS-122-2301, Illumina Inc.). A single 'A' nucleotide was added to the 3' ends of the blunt DNA fragments using a Klenow fragment (3' to 5'exo minus) enzyme. The cDNA fragments were ligated to double stranded adapters using T4 DNA Ligase. The ligated products were enriched by PCR amplification (30 sec at 98°C [10 sec at 98°C, 30 sec at 60°C, 30 sec at 72°C] x 12 cycles 5 min at 72°C). Excess of PCR primers was removed by purification using AMPure XP beads (Agencourt Biosciences Corporation). column8: Protocols: We retrospectively obtained de-identified FFPE tissue from patients who underwent ileo-colic resection surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis between 2005 and 2010. CD patient surgical resections were due to complications associated with the disease, whereas control resections were due to adenoma, carcinoma or abdominal trauma. The set of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue sections from each resection were obtained and examined by two pathologists (T.C.L. and T.S.S.) to identify the uninvolved proximal margin (terminal ileum) of each resection. These tissue sections were then further evaluated to identify those that met the histological inclusion criteria for this study. The criteria were that the sample had at least 100 well-oriented intestinal crypts (contained crypt lumens that extended from the apex to the base of the crypt) and absent/minimal active or chronic inflammatory disease (e.g., cryptitis, crypt abscess, architectural distortion, pyloric gland metaplasia, etc.).The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Washington University. Patients were recruited by the Washington University Digestive Diseases Research Core Center (DDRCC). Written informed consent was obtained from all study participants prior to inclusion in the study. For samples that met the histological inclusion criteria, two fresh, unstained 5-µm FFPE tissue sections on glass microscope slides were obtained. Slides were not baked after cutting. For each sample, the two tissue sections were scraped off of the slides using a clean razor and placed in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. The tubes were briefly centrifuged to place the sample towards the bottoms or sides of the tube. RNA extraction and DNase treatment was performed using the RNeasy FFPE kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the Xylene protocol for the paraffin removal step and 30 µL RNase-free H2O for the elution step. RNA was initially quantified by NanoDrop. Subsequent total RNA quantification and quality assessment was performed by Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). Samples were excluded from the study if >20% of the RNA fragments were >200 base pairs in length, as determined with the Bioanalyzer software. Library preparation was performed by the Genome Technology Access Center (GTAC) at Washington University. Library preparation used 150 ng of total RNA. ds-cDNA was generated using the Ovation RNA-seq FFPE system (Nugen, per manufacturer’s instructions). cDNA was blunt ended, had an A base added to the 3’ ends, and then had Illumina sequencing adapters ligated to the ends. Ligated fragments were then amplified for 12 cycles using primers incorporating unique index tags.

column13: Total RNA were extracted from tissues using the RNeasy mini Kit (Qiagen), quantified using a NanoDrop™ 8000 spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific) and quality controlled using a 2100 Electrophoresis Bioanalyzer (Agilent). Libraries of template molecules suitable for strand specific high throughput DNA sequencing were created using “TruSeq Stranded Total RNA with Ribo-Zero Gold Prep Kit” (catalog # RS-122-2301, Illumina Inc.). Briefly, the removal of cytoplasmic and mitochondrial ribosomal RNA (rRNA) was performed from 500 ng of total RNA using biotinylated, target-specific oligos combined with Ribo-Zero rRNA removal beads. The cleaved RNA fragments were copied into first strand cDNA using reverse transcriptase and random primers, followed by second strand cDNA synthesis using DNA Polymerase I and RNase H. The double stranded cDNA fragments were blunted using T4 DNA polymerase, Klenow DNA polymerase and T4 PNK. A single 'A' nucleotide was added to the 3' ends of the blunt DNA fragments using a Klenow fragment (3' to 5'exo minus) enzyme. The cDNA fragments were ligated to double stranded adapters using T4 DNA Ligase. The ligated products were enriched by PCR amplification (30 sec at 98°C [10 sec at 98°C, 30 sec at 60°C, 30 sec at 72°C] x 12 cycles 5 min at 72°C). Excess of PCR primers was removed by purification using AMPure XP beads (Agencourt Biosciences Corporation). Final cDNA libraries were quality-checked and quantified using a 2100 Electrophoresis Bioanalyzer (Agilent). The libraries were loaded in the flow cell at 7pM concentration and clusters were generated in the Cbot and sequenced in the Illumina Hiseq 2500 as paired-end 2x50 base reads following Illumina's instructions. column8: Protocols: We retrospectively obtained de-identified FFPE tissue from patients who underwent ileo-colic resection surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis between 2005 and 2010. CD patient surgical resections were due to complications associated with the disease, whereas control resections were due to adenoma, carcinoma or abdominal trauma. The set of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue sections from each resection were obtained and examined by two pathologists (T.C.L. and T.S.S.) to identify the uninvolved proximal margin (terminal ileum) of each resection. These tissue sections were then further evaluated to identify those that met the histological inclusion criteria for this study. The criteria were that the sample had at least 100 well-oriented intestinal crypts (contained crypt lumens that extended from the apex to the base of the crypt) and absent/minimal active or chronic inflammatory disease (e.g., cryptitis, crypt abscess, architectural distortion, pyloric gland metaplasia, etc.).The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Washington University. Patients were recruited by the Washington University Digestive Diseases Research Core Center (DDRCC). Written informed consent was obtained from all study participants prior to inclusion in the study. For samples that met the histological inclusion criteria, two fresh, unstained 5-µm FFPE tissue sections on glass microscope slides were obtained. Slides were not baked after cutting. For each sample, the two tissue sections were scraped off of the slides using a clean razor and placed in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. The tubes were briefly centrifuged to place the sample towards the bottoms or sides of the tube. RNA extraction and DNase treatment was performed using the RNeasy FFPE kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the Xylene protocol for the paraffin removal step and 30 µL RNase-free H2O for the elution step. RNA was initially quantified by NanoDrop. Subsequent total RNA quantification and quality assessment was performed by Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). Samples were excluded from the study if >20% of the RNA fragments were >200 base pairs in length, as determined with the Bioanalyzer software. Library preparation was performed by the Genome Technology Access Center (GTAC) at Washington University. Library preparation used 150 ng of total RNA. ds-cDNA was generated using the Ovation RNA-seq FFPE system (Nugen, per manufacturer’s instructions). cDNA was blunt ended, had an A base added to the 3’ ends, and then had Illumina sequencing adapters ligated to the ends. Ligated fragments were then amplified for 12 cycles using primers incorporating unique index tags.

column8: Protocols: We retrospectively obtained de-identified FFPE tissue from patients who underwent ileo-colic resection surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis between 2005 and 2010. CD patient surgical resections were due to complications associated with the disease, whereas control resections were due to adenoma, carcinoma or abdominal trauma. The set of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue sections from each resection were obtained and examined by two pathologists (T.C.L. and T.S.S.) to identify the uninvolved proximal margin (terminal ileum) of each resection. These tissue sections were then further evaluated to identify those that met the histological inclusion criteria for this study. The criteria were that the sample had at least 100 well-oriented intestinal crypts (contained crypt lumens that extended from the apex to the base of the crypt) and absent/minimal active or chronic inflammatory disease (e.g., cryptitis, crypt abscess, architectural distortion, pyloric gland metaplasia, etc.).The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Washington University. Patients were recruited by the Washington University Digestive Diseases Research Core Center (DDRCC). Written informed consent was obtained from all study participants prior to inclusion in the study. For samples that met the histological inclusion criteria, two fresh, unstained 5-µm FFPE tissue sections on glass microscope slides were obtained. Slides were not baked after cutting. For each sample, the two tissue sections were scraped off of the slides using a clean razor and placed in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. The tubes were briefly centrifuged to place the sample towards the bottoms or sides of the tube. RNA extraction and DNase treatment was performed using the RNeasy FFPE kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the Xylene protocol for the paraffin removal step and 30 µL RNase-free H2O for the elution step. RNA was initially quantified by NanoDrop. Subsequent total RNA quantification and quality assessment was performed by Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). Samples were excluded from the study if >20% of the RNA fragments were >200 base pairs in length, as determined with the Bioanalyzer software. Library preparation was performed by the Genome Technology Access Center (GTAC) at Washington University. Library preparation used 150 ng of total RNA. ds-cDNA was generated using the Ovation RNA-seq FFPE system (Nugen, per manufacturer’s instructions). cDNA was blunt ended, had an A base added to the 3’ ends, and then had Illumina sequencing adapters ligated to the ends. Ligated fragments were then amplified for 12 cycles using primers incorporating unique index tags.

column13: Total RNA were extracted from tissues using the RNeasy mini Kit (Qiagen), quantified using a NanoDrop™ 8000 spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific) and quality controlled using a 2100 Electrophoresis Bioanalyzer (Agilent). Libraries of template molecules suitable for strand specific high throughput DNA sequencing were created using “TruSeq Stranded Total RNA with Ribo-Zero Gold Prep Kit” (catalog # RS-122-2301, Illumina Inc.). Briefly, the removal of cytoplasmic and mitochondrial ribosomal RNA (rRNA) was performed from 500 ng of total RNA using biotinylated, target-specific oligos combined with Ribo-Zero rRNA removal beads. Following purification, the RNA was fragmented using divalent cations under elevated temperature. The cleaved RNA fragments were copied into first strand cDNA using reverse transcriptase and random primers, followed by second strand cDNA synthesis using DNA Polymerase I and RNase H. The double stranded cDNA fragments were blunted using T4 DNA polymerase, Klenow DNA polymerase and T4 PNK. A single 'A' nucleotide was added to the 3' ends of the blunt DNA fragments using a Klenow fragment (3' to 5'exo minus) enzyme. The cDNA fragments were ligated to double stranded adapters using T4 DNA Ligase. The ligated products were enriched by PCR amplification (30 sec at 98°C [10 sec at 98°C, 30 sec at 60°C, 30 sec at 72°C] x 12 cycles 5 min at 72°C). Excess of PCR primers was removed by purification using AMPure XP beads (Agencourt Biosciences Corporation). Final cDNA libraries were quality-checked and quantified using a 2100 Electrophoresis Bioanalyzer (Agilent). The libraries were loaded in the flow cell at 7pM concentration and clusters were generated in the Cbot and sequenced in the Illumina Hiseq 2500 as paired-end 2x50 base reads following Illumina's instructions. Image analysis and base calling were performed using RTA 1.17.20 and CASAVA 1.8.2.

column8: Protocols: We retrospectively obtained de-identified FFPE tissue from patients who underwent ileo-colic resection surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis between 2005 and 2010. CD patient surgical resections were due to complications associated with the disease, whereas control resections were due to adenoma, carcinoma or abdominal trauma. The set of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue sections from each resection were obtained and examined by two pathologists (T.C.L. and T.S.S.) to identify the uninvolved proximal margin (terminal ileum) of each resection. These tissue sections were then further evaluated to identify those that met the histological inclusion criteria for this study. The criteria were that the sample had at least 100 well-oriented intestinal crypts (contained crypt lumens that extended from the apex to the base of the crypt) and absent/minimal active or chronic inflammatory disease (e.g., cryptitis, crypt abscess, architectural distortion, pyloric gland metaplasia, etc.).The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Washington University. Patients were recruited by the Washington University Digestive Diseases Research Core Center (DDRCC). Written informed consent was obtained from all study participants prior to inclusion in the study. For samples that met the histological inclusion criteria, two fresh, unstained 5-µm FFPE tissue sections on glass microscope slides were obtained. Slides were not baked after cutting. For each sample, the two tissue sections were scraped off of the slides using a clean razor and placed in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. The tubes were briefly centrifuged to place the sample towards the bottoms or sides of the tube. RNA extraction and DNase treatment was performed using the RNeasy FFPE kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the Xylene protocol for the paraffin removal step and 30 µL RNase-free H2O for the elution step. RNA was initially quantified by NanoDrop. Subsequent total RNA quantification and quality assessment was performed by Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). Samples were excluded from the study if >20% of the RNA fragments were >200 base pairs in length, as determined with the Bioanalyzer software. Library preparation was performed by the Genome Technology Access Center (GTAC) at Washington University. Library preparation used 150 ng of total RNA. ds-cDNA was generated using the Ovation RNA-seq FFPE system (Nugen, per manufacturer’s instructions). cDNA was blunt ended, had an A base added to the 3’ ends, and then had Illumina sequencing adapters ligated to the ends. Ligated fragments were then amplified for 12 cycles using primers incorporating unique index tags.

column8: Protocols: We retrospectively obtained de-identified FFPE tissue from patients who underwent ileo-colic resection surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis between 2005 and 2010. CD patient surgical resections were due to complications associated with the disease, whereas control resections were due to adenoma, carcinoma or abdominal trauma. The set of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue sections from each resection were obtained and examined by two pathologists (T.C.L. and T.S.S.) to identify the uninvolved proximal margin (terminal ileum) of each resection. These tissue sections were then further evaluated to identify those that met the histological inclusion criteria for this study. The criteria were that the sample had at least 100 well-oriented intestinal crypts (contained crypt lumens that extended from the apex to the base of the crypt) and absent/minimal active or chronic inflammatory disease (e.g., cryptitis, crypt abscess, architectural distortion, pyloric gland metaplasia, etc.).The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Washington University. Patients were recruited by the Washington University Digestive Diseases Research Core Center (DDRCC). Written informed consent was obtained from all study participants prior to inclusion in the study. For samples that met the histological inclusion criteria, two fresh, unstained 5-µm FFPE tissue sections on glass microscope slides were obtained. Slides were not baked after cutting. For each sample, the two tissue sections were scraped off of the slides using a clean razor and placed in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. The tubes were briefly centrifuged to place the sample towards the bottoms or sides of the tube. RNA extraction and DNase treatment was performed using the RNeasy FFPE kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using the Xylene protocol for the paraffin removal step and 30 µL RNase-free H2O for the elution step. RNA was initially quantified by NanoDrop. Subsequent total RNA quantification and quality assessment was performed by Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). Samples were excluded from the study if >20% of the RNA fragments were >200 base pairs in length, as determined with the Bioanalyzer software. Library preparation was performed by the Genome Technology Access Center (GTAC) at Washington University. Library preparation used 150 ng of total RNA. ds-cDNA was generated using the Ovation RNA-seq FFPE system (Nugen, per manufacturer’s instructions). cDNA was blunt ended, had an A base added to the 3’ ends, and then had Illumina sequencing adapters ligated to the ends. Ligated fragments were then amplified for 12 cycles using primers incorporating unique index tags.

column13: Fetal tissue samples <100 mg in size were placed into DNase- and RNase-free 1.5 ml microfuge tubes containing 1 ml of RNAlater RNA Stabilization Reagent (Qiagen) within 1 hour of the pregnancy termination procedure. After storage at room temperature for a period of 24-72 h, excess RNAlater was removed from the microfuge tubes and the samples were placed in the -80oC freezer for storage until RNA isolation was performed. The tissues were lysed in mirVana (Life Technologies) lysis buffer, using a Mini-Beadbeater-16 (Biospec), with agitation for 1 min in the presence of 1 mm zirconia beads. Samples were then centrifuged at maximum speed in a tabletop microcentrifuge for 1 min and the lysed solution was transferred to a fresh microfuge tube. The remainder of the extraction was per the manufacturer's protocol for the mirVana kit (Life Technologies). Following RNA isolation (mirVana miRNA Isolation Kit, Life Technologies, Inc.), the RNA was quantified (Qubit RNA Assay Kit, Life Technologies, Inc.), and quality controlled (RNA6000 Nano Kit and BioAnalyzer 2100, Agilent). 200 ng to 1000 ng was used as input for the Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA with Ribo-Zero Gold sample prep kit (Illumina, Inc.) and sequencing libraries were created according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Briefly, first both cytoplasmic and mitochondrial rRNA was removed by selectively hybridizing biotinylated probes to target sequences and using magnetic beads to capture the bound products. Following rRNA removal, the RNA was fragmented and copied into first strand cDNA using random primers and reverse transcriptase. Next, second strand cDNA synthesis was completed using DNA Polymerase I and RNase H. The cDNA was then ligated to Illumina supplied adapters and enriched with PCR to create the final cDNA libraries. The libraries were then pooled and sequenced on a HiSeq 2000 (Illumina, Inc.) instrument as per manufacturer’s instructions. Sequencing was performed up to 2 X 101 cycles.
